name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Democrat Lisa Kinney raised under $20,000 with no outside support
Republican Chuck Gray has strong fundraising and outside spending
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~98%
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this seat effectively unwinnable for a Democrat, and the resource gap is extreme: Gray has raised $1.6 million with outside backing while Kinney has raised under $20,000. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe R.
model.watch: A major scandal or third-party surge could shave the margin, but nothing in the evidence suggests the seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. With Harriet Hageman retiring to run for Senate, Republican Chuck Gray enters the general election as the heavy favorite. He has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from more than $1.6 million in outside support, while outside groups have spent over $700,000 opposing him.

Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 and has no outside spending on her behalf, leaving her with minimal resources to compete statewide. Prediction markets put the Republican's chances near 98 percent. The forecast rates the race Safe Republican, with Gray expected to win by roughly 20 points.
